description: SOMOS O DO FIRJAN SENAI RJ ESTUDANTES DE LOGÍSTICA
summary:
Mars Walk Planner is an interactive, layered map of Jezero Crater that helps astronauts plan a safe and scientific walk on Mars. We integrated data from multiple NASA missions, including HiRISE and MOLA for terrain, CRISM for mineralogy, Curiosity and MAVEN for weather and radiation, and Mars Odyssey for resources. Users can toggle each layer, view a round-trip route, and see a logistics panel that estimates distance, walking time, oxygen, water, and safety margin.

This addresses the challenge by combining separate datasets into one clear view that supports route planning, safety decisions, and new science along the way. Our logistics approach treats the walk like a supply chain: limited resources, risk, and a mandatory return.

It matters because the first humans on Mars will need reliable, easy-to-read information to complete missions quickly and safely. A tool like this can reduce risk and help explorers focus on discovery.
details:
What it does and how it works
Mars Walk Planner is an interactive, layered map of Jezero Crater. Users can toggle five layers: terrain and slope, mineralogy and science points, weather and radiation, water-related resources, and safety (hazards, shelters, and return route). The map shows a round-trip route (12.1 km, 4 waypoints) and a logistics panel that estimates distance, walking time, oxygen, water, and safety margin. The user can change the number of astronauts and the walk duration, and the app warns if the remaining oxygen is not enough for the return.

Benefits
It puts data from several NASA missions into one clear view, so an explorer does not need to check separate sources. It supports faster, safer decisions and helps balance risk, distance, and science value.

Intended impact
To help future crews plan Mars walks more safely and efficiently, and to show how logistics thinking (limited resources, risk, and a mandatory return) can support space exploration. It can also work as an educational tool for students.

Tools and technology

  • Base44 (AI-assisted app builder) for the interactive web app
  • NASA Mars Trek and NASA open data from HiRISE, MOLA, CRISM, Curiosity (REMS), MAVEN, and Mars Odyssey
  • Gamma and PowerPoint for the demo presentation
  • AI assistance (Claude) for brainstorming, text, and prompt writing. All data sources were reviewed by the team.

Creativity
We treated a Mars walk as a supply chain problem. Oxygen, water, and time work like inventory with a safety stock, and the return route is a non-negotiable requirement. This logistics view is not common in Mars mapping tools.

Factors our team considered

  • Safety: slopes, boulder fields, hazard zones, and shelters
  • Science value: routes connecting the river delta, crater rim, and mineral sites
  • Resources: oxygen, water, and a return margin
  • Data reliability: we used NASA sources and sample values, which need validation for real missions
  • Clarity: simple toggles and a bilingual interface (English and Portuguese)
  • Teamwork: six members, each with a defined role

Antes de enviar

  • Confirmem se o app é mesmo bilíngue e se o painel de logística funciona como descrito.
  • A linha sobre o uso de IA é importante para a transparência. Mantenham.
